svg.text: no upstream build, distributions only; no optimizations

g.title: LangChain - green (critical) Release: upstream Gap: LangChain ships exclusively as a `py3-none-any` wheel for every release; the live PyPI check on 2026-08-28 confirms langchain-1.3.18 carries the `py3-none-any` tag, so `pip install langchain` works on riscv64 without modification. Under Step 0 of the color model, a pure-Python architecture-independent wheel is classified green with no CI requirement. LangChain contains no compiled extensions, SIMD code, or architecture-specific paths; the report and live check are fully consistent. See [PyPI langchain 1.3.18](https://pypi.org/project/langchain/1.3.18/).

LangGraph - green (critical) Release: upstream Gap: LangGraph ships exclusively as a `py3-none-any` universal wheel on PyPI, confirmed at version 1.2.11 by live PyPI JSON API check on 2026-08-28. The color-coding Step 0 shortcut applies: no compiled, architecture-specific code exists in the project (confirmed by full code search in [reports/langgraph.md](reports/langgraph.md)), so riscv64 support is guaranteed by construction. LangChain Inc. publishes directly to PyPI, satisfying the release-provider requirement for green.

langchain-core - green (critical) Release: upstream Gap: langchain-core ships exclusively as a `py3-none-any` wheel -- confirmed: [`langchain_core-1.6.1-py3-none-any.whl`](https://pypi.org/pypi/langchain-core/1.6.1/json) uploaded 2026-08-27, with no platform-specific variants. The build backend is `hatchling` (pure Python, no native extensions), confirmed via the [pyproject.toml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/langchain/master/libs/core/pyproject.toml). Under Step 0 of the color model, a pure-Python `py3-none-any` wheel runs on riscv64 by construction and is classified green without requiring riscv64 CI; the optimization-purpose modifier does not apply to an orchestration library.

langsmith - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: The core `langsmith` package ships exclusively as a `py3-none-any` wheel (confirmed at [PyPI langsmith 0.11.2](https://pypi.org/pypi/langsmith/json): two artifacts, `langsmith-0.11.2-py3-none-any.whl` and the sdist), triggering the Step 0 architecture-independent shortcut -- green with no CI requirement. The optional `langsmith[langsmith_pyo3]` Rust extension extra publishes only x86_64, aarch64, and macOS arm64 wheels (no riscv64), but this extra is explicitly optional and not required for core tracing and observability. No riscv64-specific compiled artifacts are present in the main package, and `release_provider` is upstream (langchain-ai on PyPI).

langgraph-checkpoint - green (critical) Release: upstream Gap: langgraph-checkpoint 4.2.0 ships exclusively as a `py3-none-any` wheel confirmed at [PyPI langgraph-checkpoint 4.2.0](https://pypi.org/pypi/langgraph-checkpoint/json). Per Step 0, the package contains no compiled code of its own and installs on riscv64 by construction; upstream (LangChain Inc.) publishes directly to PyPI. The required dependency `ormsgpack>=1.12.0` has no prebuilt riscv64 wheel and requires a Rust source build, but this is a dependency-level friction issue and does not change the color of langgraph-checkpoint itself under the Step 0 rule.

langgraph-prebuilt - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: langgraph-prebuilt ships exclusively as a [py3-none-any wheel on PyPI](https://pypi.org/pypi/langgraph-prebuilt/json) (v1.1.0), confirmed by live check: the package uses hatchling with no compiled extensions, and all source files under `libs/prebuilt/langgraph/prebuilt/` are pure Python. Under Step 0 of the color model, a py3-none-any wheel is architecture-independent and runs on riscv64 by construction. The wheel is published directly by upstream (langchain-ai) to PyPI.

langgraph-sdk - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: Step 0 applies: all releases on PyPI ship exclusively as `py3-none-any` wheels (confirmed for both the cited v0.1.70 and the current v0.4.4 at [PyPI](https://pypi.org/pypi/langgraph-sdk/json)). The source tree under `libs/sdk-py/` contains only `.py` files and uses `hatchling` as its build backend with no compiled extensions, confirming the package is architecture-independent and installs on riscv64 by construction with no modifications needed.

vLLM (CPU backend) - orange (critical) Release: none Gap: vLLM has no riscv64 CI across all 10 GitHub Actions workflow files (confirmed live 2026-08-28) and no riscv64 release artifact from any source -- PyPI v0.28.0 ships only x86_64 and aarch64 wheels, RISE does not package vLLM, and vLLM is absent from Debian, Ubuntu 24.04, and Arch RISC-V. The proposed `color_case: downstream-only` is factually wrong: "downstream-only" requires a downstream distro or third party to actually ship the package, which none does. The correct call is plain orange (no CI, no distribution floor at all) with an empty color_case. The color itself (orange) is upheld; the sub-type label is corrected. See [PyPI vllm](https://pypi.org/pypi/vllm/json) and [.github/workflows listing](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/.github/workflows).

llama.cpp - blue (critical) Release: Debian Gap: The `ubuntu-cpu-riscv64-native` job in [build-riscv.yml](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp/blob/master/.github/workflows/build-riscv.yml) runs `ctest -L main --verbose --timeout 900` on RISE bare-metal `ubuntu-24.04-riscv` runners on every push to master, confirming native test execution -- not build-only. No upstream riscv64 release binaries exist (issue [#20988](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp/issues/20988) closed not-planned; PR [#20991](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp/pull/20991) open but unmerged); Debian sid is the only pre-built source. As an optimization-purpose project, the RVV optimization level is partial: vec dot covers all major quant formats and repack GEMM/GEMV covers Q4_0, Q4_K, Q8_0, Q2_K, IQ4_NL (the dominant inference formats), but Q3_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q5_0, Q5_1 repack paths remain scalar (draft PR [#23745](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp/pull/23745) still open as of 2026-08-28), capping the grade at blue.

ExecuTorch - blue (optional) Release: none Gap: The [riscv64.yml](https://github.com/pytorch/executorch/blob/main/.github/workflows/riscv64.yml) workflow calls `_test_riscv.yml`, which cross-compiles executor_runner and runs it under `qemu-riscv64-static`, checking for "Test_result: PASS" via `run.sh` -- confirmed genuine test execution, not build-only. Latest release v1.4.1 has only `.pack` and `.pdsc` assets with no riscv64 binary, PR #19917 (baremetal bare-metal tests) remains open and unmerged, and no riscv64 artifact appears on PyPI, Ubuntu, Debian, Arch RISC-V, or the RISE wheel builder -- so the release-provider prerequisite for green is not met.

FastAPI - green (critical) Release: upstream Gap: FastAPI ships exclusively as a [py3-none-any wheel on PyPI](https://pypi.org/pypi/fastapi/json) (version 0.141.1, confirmed live), with no compiled extensions and `pdm.backend` as its build backend. Step 0 of the color model applies: the architecture-independent pure-Python package installs on riscv64 by construction. The [publish workflow](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/master/.github/workflows/publish.yml) runs a single `uv build` on ubuntu-latest producing the universal wheel; upstream publishes it directly to PyPI, satisfying the release_provider prerequisite for green. Note: upstream CI (test.yml) runs only on ubuntu/windows/macos -- there is no riscv64 CI runner -- but this is irrelevant under Step 0, which grants green without requiring riscv64 CI for architecture-independent packages.

Starlette - green (critical) Release: upstream Gap: Starlette ships exclusively as a `py3-none-any` wheel (confirmed for the latest release [starlette-1.6.0-py3-none-any.whl](https://pypi.org/pypi/starlette/1.6.0/json)); pyproject.toml uses hatchling with no C extensions, Cython, or compiled artifacts. Step 0 applies: architecture-independent, runs on riscv64 by construction. The proposed classification referenced stale version 0.46.2 (April 2025); the current version is 1.6.0 (published 2026-08-08), but the classification color is unchanged.
uvicorn - grey (critical) Release: none

PyTorch (CPU eager inference) - yellow (critical) Release: Debian Gap: The in-tree [`.github/workflows/riscv64.yml`](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/.github/workflows/riscv64.yml) contains exactly one job (`pytorch-linux-noble-riscv64-py3_12-gcc14-cross-build`) calling `_linux-build.yml` with no test matrix, confirmed build-only CI (verified 2026-08-28). ATen CPU vectorization has zero RVV dispatch: the `CPUCapability` enum (DispatchStub.h, verified 2026-08-28) lists DEFAULT/VSX/ZVECTOR/SVE256/SVE128/AVX2/AVX512 but no RVV entry, and PR #175746 (RVV ATen vec) was closed without merging (state: closed, merged_at: null). One RVV kernel exists (DepthwiseConvKernel.cpp, 76 RVV lines from PR #127867) giving a minimal optimization level that caps at yellow - matching the primary CI grade. RISE out-of-tree CI (riseproject-dev/pytorch-ci) now has a test job on native riscv64 hardware but is conditional (`enable-tests` input), out-of-tree, and does not gate upstream PRs, so it does not raise the upstream CI tier. Debian sid ships v2.12.0+dfsg2-4 as the only binary release channel; no riscv64 wheel on PyPI or RISE.

HuggingFace Transformers - green (critical) Release: upstream Gap: HuggingFace Transformers is a pure-Python library that ships exclusively as a `py3-none-any` wheel, confirmed live against the [PyPI JSON API](https://pypi.org/pypi/transformers/json) on 2026-08-28 showing `transformers-5.16.1-py3-none-any.whl` as the sole wheel artifact. Under Step 0 of the color model it is architecture-independent and runs on riscv64 by construction. The `setup.py` has no `ext_modules`, no `Extension()`, no Cython, and no `build_ext`; the `pyproject.toml` is linting-only; Step 2 (optimization-purpose modifier) does not apply because all compute is delegated to backend frameworks.

Accelerate - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: Accelerate 1.14.0 ships exclusively as a `py3-none-any` wheel on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/pypi/accelerate/json) with no compiled extensions (setup.py contains no `ext_modules`). Under Step 0 of the color model, architecture-independent packages are classified green -- they run on riscv64 by construction, inheriting RISC-V support from the Python runtime. Accelerate is not optimization-purpose (it is a distributed-training abstraction layer, not a SIMD/performance library), so the Step 2 modifier does not apply.

HuggingFace Hub - green (critical) Release: upstream Gap: HuggingFace Hub ships exclusively as a `py3-none-any` wheel with no compiled extensions -- confirmed by [PyPI metadata](https://pypi.org/pypi/huggingface_hub/json) showing v1.29.0 (2026-08-27) as `huggingface_hub-1.29.0-py3-none-any.whl` only, and by [setup.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/huggingface_hub/main/setup.py) which contains no `ext_modules`, CFFI, Cython, or Rust extensions. Per Step 0 of the color model, a pure-Python `py3-none-any` package is architecture-independent and runs on riscv64 by construction; upstream publishes directly on PyPI.

HuggingFace Tokenizers - yellow (critical) Release: upstream Gap: Live inspection of [CI.yml](https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers/blob/main/.github/workflows/CI.yml) confirms the riscv64 matrix entry has only "Build wheels" and "Upload wheels" steps -- no test execution step exists for riscv64 on any trigger. Despite this, upstream publishes a `manylinux_2_31_riscv64` wheel to PyPI since v0.23.1 (Apr 27, 2026, confirmed via PyPI JSON API). Yellow is correct: build-only CI caps at yellow regardless of release availability; green requires test execution. The optimization-purpose modifier does not apply because tokenizers is pure scalar Rust with no arch-specific code paths and its value proposition is correctness, not speed over a reference.

SentencePiece - blue (critical) Release: RISE Gap: The live [cross_build.yml](https://github.com/google/sentencepiece/blob/master/.github/workflows/cross_build.yml) (verified 2026-08-28) confirms riscv64 is in the arch matrix and the "Test on QEMU" step (`qemu-riscv64 ... src/spm_test`) is only skipped for sparc64 and sh4 -- riscv64 executes the full test suite. No riscv64 wheel appears in the v0.2.2 release assets (published 2026-07-12); `wheel.yml` still has `CIBW_ARCHS_LINUX: auto` with no riscv64 entry. Riscv64 wheels remain available only from the RISE unofficial wheel builder registry.

Tiktoken - yellow (optional) Release: RISE Gap: Upstream CI ([build_wheels.yml](https://github.com/openai/tiktoken/blob/main/.github/workflows/build_wheels.yml)) has no riscv64 job (confirmed live 2026-08-28), and PyPI carries no riscv64 wheel for the latest version 0.14.0 (released 2026-08-17). Debian sid builds `python3-tiktoken 0.12.0-2` on native riscv64 hardware (`rv-osuosl-04`, status: Installed) from unpatched upstream source (the three Debian patches lower dependency versions and adjust build metadata, none are riscv64-specific), applying the clean-distro-build yellow floor. RISE (via BayLibre) also publishes binary wheels at its GitLab PyPI index; upstream [PR #506](https://github.com/openai/tiktoken/pull/506) adding riscv64 CI remains open and unmerged as of 2026-08-28.

NumPy - yellow (critical) Release: RISE Gap: The native riscv64 CI workflow ([linux_riscv64.yml](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/main/.github/workflows/linux_riscv64.yml)) is confirmed build-only: `cibuildwheel` runs with no `CIBW_TEST_COMMAND`, no `spin test` step, and no `pytest` invocation -- the job is named "Build wheel" exclusively. QEMU CI ([linux_qemu.yml](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/main/.github/workflows/linux_qemu.yml)) does run tests via `spin test` but carries `continue-on-error: true` making it non-blocking. No upstream riscv64 wheel exists on PyPI (NumPy 2.5.2 has zero riscv64 entries); RISE provides wheels up to 2.5.2. The NPYV layer has no RVV backend, so all ~22 arithmetic, transcendental, reduction, and comparison ufunc kernels fall back to scalar C -- this "minimal" optimization level caps the grade at yellow, consistent with the CI-based grade already being yellow.

SafeTensors - yellow (critical) Release: upstream Gap: The live CI workflow file at `.github/workflows/python-release.yml` confirms the riscv64 matrix entry contains only checkout, maturin-action cross-build, and upload-artifact steps -- no pytest, no QEMU, no test execution -- identical to what the 2026-06-17 report documented. An official `safetensors-0.8.0-cp310-abi3-manylinux_2_31_riscv64.whl` is published to [PyPI by upstream](https://pypi.org/pypi/safetensors/json), but publishing a wheel without test execution does not satisfy the green criterion; per the color model, green requires the test suite to pass in CI, and yellow explicitly allows "no / either" in the artifact column. The project has no architecture-specific code on any platform (pure portable Rust + PyO3), so the optimization-purpose modifier (Step 2) does not apply and cannot cap the color further.

ONNX Runtime (CPU EP) - yellow (optional) Release: Debian Gap: No riscv64 CI exists in microsoft/onnxruntime, confirmed live by listing all 50+ workflow files under .github/workflows/ with no riscv/rv64 hits. Debian sid ships onnxruntime 1.23.2+dfsg-6+b5 for riscv64 (built on rv-osuosl-01, status "Installed"), and the Debian packaging repository at salsa.debian.org contains 18-19 patches none of which are riscv64-specific (names cover ARM32 test disable, Power10, GCC 14 fixes, system-library substitutions, and Eigen compatibility -- no RISC-V targeting). The optimization-purpose modifier (11 RVV MLAS kernel files = Partial coverage) caps at blue, which is above yellow and therefore does not lower the distro-floor yellow grade.
FAISS (CPU) - grey (critical) Release: none

OpenBLAS - blue (critical) Release: none Gap: Upstream CI at [OpenMathLib/OpenBLAS `riscv64_vector.yml`](https://github.com/OpenMathLib/OpenBLAS/blob/develop/.github/workflows/riscv64_vector.yml) builds and runs BLAS L1/L2/L3 and CBLAS tests under QEMU for ZVL128B, ZVL256B, and DYNAMIC_ARCH targets, confirming blue (not yellow). No upstream riscv64 binary release exists. Optimization level is partial: GEMM fully covered with RVV intrinsics; TRSM now has partial RVV coverage (STRSM all variants, D/C/ZTRSM RN+RT via RVV) in v0.3.34 after PR #5830 merged 2026-08-16, but DTRSM/CTRSM/ZTRSM LN+LT cases still fall back to generic C - partial optimization caps at blue, matching the primary grade.

Eigen - blue (optional) Release: none Gap: Upstream CI on [ci/test.linux.gitlab-ci.yml](https://gitlab.com/libeigen/eigen/-/raw/master/ci/test.linux.gitlab-ci.yml) runs full CTest suites on native SpacemiT riscv64 hardware (gcc-15 and clang-21 as of 2026-08-28, upgraded from gcc-14/clang-18), but all riscv64 jobs carry `allow_failure: true` and no released version (latest 5.0.1, 2025-11-08) contains the RVV backend -- it is master-only. The RVV backend covers primary hot paths (GEMM, packet math for int/float/FP16/BF16/complex) qualifying as partial optimization, capped at blue; transcendental functions (exp/log/sin/cos) and masked partial-packet tails (`has_packet_segment`) still use scalar fallback.

oneDNN (DNNL) - blue (critical) Release: none Gap: The `ci-riscv.yml` workflow file (verified live 2026-08-28) contains a distinct `test` job with a "Run oneDNN tests" step executing SMOKE tests under QEMU at vlen=128 and vlen=256, confirming genuine test execution not merely a build step. No upstream binary artifacts exist: all GitHub releases are source-only tags and no riscv64 PyPI wheel is present, so release_provider is none. As an optimization-purpose library, the rv64 directory (confirmed live: `src/cpu/rv64/`) contains JIT RVV implementations covering the primary hot paths (f32/f16/bf16 conv, matmul, GEMM, pooling, softmax, layernorm, eltwise) via xbyak_riscv; INT8 conv/matmul (s8/u8) is absent, placing optimization at partial and capping at blue -- the CI-derived primary grade of blue is confirmed.

XNNPACK - blue (critical) Release: none Gap: The `cmake-linux-riscv64` CI job runs tests via `ctest --label-exclude operator` (not build-only), and the job has been passing since at least 2026-07-08 (verified 2026-08-26 run [#33000168130](https://github.com/google/XNNPACK/actions/runs/33000168130)). The root cause of issue #9886 - unconditional `xnn_arch_riscv_vector_fp16_arith` flag set without Zvfh detection - was fixed in commit `aee6b1b3` (2026-04-07) adding `supports_rvv_fp16()` runtime probe; issue #9886 remains open but the bug is resolved. Optimization level is partial (206 production RVV/Zvfh kernel files covering GEMM, DWCONV, elementwise, reductions; no BF16; no hand-written assembly; narrower MR/NR than arm64), which caps at blue - matching the CI-based grade. No upstream riscv64 release artifacts exist, excluding green.
FBGEMM - grey (optional) Release: none

SLEEF - blue (critical) Release: debian Gap: The [Jenkinsfile](https://github.com/shibatch/sleef/blob/master/Jenkinsfile) contains two riscv64 stages (agent label `riscv && ubuntu24`) that both run `ctest -j $(nproc)` with `-DSLEEF_ENFORCE_TESTER4=True`, confirming actual math correctness test execution (not build-only) on a native riscv64 agent. The [helperrvv.h](https://github.com/shibatch/sleef/blob/master/src/arch/helperrvv.h) RVV v1.0 backend covers all in-scope SP and DP transcendentals with RVVM1 and RVVM2 LMUL configurations, matching arm64 SVE coverage and yielding a "full" optimization level with no downgrade cap. Upstream ships source-only; the consumable riscv64 binary is provided by Debian sid (3.9.0-1), not upstream, so green is not applicable.

Pydantic - yellow (critical) Release: upstream Gap: The `core-build` CI job ([ci.yml line 96](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml)) cross-compiles riscv64 wheels via maturin and uploads them to PyPI; pydantic-core 2.48.0 ships 8 riscv64 manylinux wheels on PyPI. However, the `core-test-builds-arch` job - which runs `pytest tests/pydantic_core` via QEMU for non-native targets - covers only armv7, s390x, ppc64le, and aarch64; riscv64 is absent from that test matrix. The single occurrence of "riscv" in the entire CI file is the build target, confirming build-only CI with no test execution on riscv64.

httpx - green (critical) Release: upstream Gap: httpx ships a single `py3-none-any` wheel ([httpx-0.28.1-py3-none-any.whl](https://pypi.org/pypi/httpx/json)) published by upstream on PyPI, with no compiled artifacts. Step 0 of the color model applies: pure-Python architecture-independent package runs on riscv64 by construction. The `pyproject.toml` uses `hatchling` with no C extension build hooks, and all core runtime dependencies (`certifi`, `httpcore`, `anyio`, `idna`) are likewise pure Python.

requests - green (critical) Release: upstream Gap: Step 0 applies: requests ships exclusively as a `py3-none-any` wheel with no compiled code. Live PyPI check confirms the only release artifact for v2.34.2 is `requests-2.34.2-py3-none-any.whl`, and `pyproject.toml` has no `ext_modules` or compiled extensions. Published directly by PSF (upstream) at [pypi.org/project/requests](https://pypi.org/pypi/requests/json).

aiohttp - yellow (optional) Release: upstream Gap: Upstream CI builds riscv64 wheels via QEMU using cibuildwheel (both manylinux and musllinux) as confirmed by [ci-cd.yml](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/blob/master/.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml) lines 692-695, but `test-command = ""` in [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/blob/master/pyproject.toml) disables all test execution globally, and the [reusable-cibuildwheel.yml](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/blob/master/.github/workflows/reusable-cibuildwheel.yml) workflow contains only a build step with no test phase. Upstream publishes 12 riscv64 wheels (manylinux and musllinux, Python 3.10-3.14) directly to PyPI via the `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` deploy job, confirmed for version 3.14.3 by the [PyPI JSON API](https://pypi.org/pypi/aiohttp/json).

typing-extensions - green (critical) Release: upstream Gap: typing-extensions ships exclusively as a `py3-none-any` wheel (verified live at [PyPI 4.16.0](https://pypi.org/pypi/typing-extensions/json): single wheel `typing_extensions-4.16.0-py3-none-any.whl`, no compiled artifacts). Under Step 0 of the color model, a pure-Python `py3-none-any` wheel is architecture-independent and installs on riscv64 by construction; no riscv64 CI is required. The [publish.yml](https://github.com/python/typing_extensions/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml) workflow confirms upstream publishes directly to PyPI via trusted publishing on release events, satisfying the `release_provider: upstream` prerequisite for green.

packaging - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: packaging 26.3 ships exclusively as a [py3-none-any wheel on PyPI](https://pypi.org/pypi/packaging/json), confirmed by live PyPI API check. The repo contains no C/C++/Cython files other than a test fixture (tests/hello-world.c) that is explicitly excluded from the sdist and wheel. Step 0 of the color model applies: a pure-Python py3-none-any wheel is architecture-independent and installs on riscv64 by construction; no riscv64 CI is required.
filelock - grey (optional) Release: none

fsspec - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: fsspec ships exclusively as a `py3-none-any` wheel on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/pypi/fsspec/json) (latest: 2026.7.0), confirmed live. A full recursive scan of the git tree found zero compiled source files (.c, .pyx, .rs, .cpp) across all 173 files, and `pyproject.toml` uses pure `hatchling` with no compiled-extension hooks. Under Step 0, a pure-Python architecture-independent wheel runs on riscv64 by construction; no riscv64 CI is required for green.
tenacity - grey (optional) Release: none

tqdm - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: tqdm 4.70.0 ships a single [py3-none-any wheel on PyPI](https://pypi.org/pypi/tqdm/json) with no compiled artifacts: the source tree contains no .c, .pyx, or extension module declarations, and pyproject.toml uses only pure setuptools with no C extension build steps. Under Step 0 of the color model, a py3-none-any wheel is architecture-independent and runs on riscv64 by construction, qualifying for green without any CI requirement. Adversarial check confirmed: live PyPI API query verified the sole wheel artifact is py3-none-any and no riscv64-specific or compiled wheels exist.

networkx - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: NetworkX 3.6.1 ships exclusively as a [py3-none-any wheel on PyPI](https://pypi.org/pypi/networkx/json) with no compiled extensions (build backend is plain setuptools, no C/Cython/Rust files in the repository). Under Step 0 of the color model, a pure-Python architecture-independent package runs on riscv64 by construction and classifies as green without penalizing it for lacking riscv64 CI. Upstream publishes the wheel directly on PyPI, satisfying the release_provider prerequisite for green.

sympy - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: SymPy ships exclusively as a `py3-none-any` wheel on PyPI (1.14.0, uploaded 2025-04-27 by upstream), containing no compiled C/C++ extensions - confirmed by inspecting all release artifacts at [PyPI](https://pypi.org/pypi/sympy/json) and searching the repository for `ext_modules`, cffi, and Cython (zero results). Step 0 of the color model applies: a pure-Python `py3-none-any` wheel is architecture-independent and runs on riscv64 by construction.

OpenTelemetry API - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: The package ships only a `py3-none-any` wheel with no compiled artifacts (confirmed by inspecting the 47-file wheel: zero `.so`, `.pyd`, `.dll`, `.c`, or `.cpp` entries). Step 0 applies: architecture-independent pure-Python wheel runs on riscv64 by construction. The release is published directly by upstream (PyPI author: `cncf-opentelemetry-contributors@lists.cncf.io`), satisfying the `release_provider: upstream` prerequisite for green. See [PyPI opentelemetry-api 1.44.0](https://pypi.org/pypi/opentelemetry-api/1.44.0/json).

OpenTelemetry SDK - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: The [opentelemetry-sdk 1.44.0 release on PyPI](https://pypi.org/pypi/opentelemetry-sdk/json) ships exclusively as `opentelemetry_sdk-1.44.0-py3-none-any.whl` with no compiled C/Rust extensions (confirmed via `pyproject.toml` which uses `hatchling` with no `extension_modules`). Under Step 0 of the color model, a pure-Python `py3-none-any` wheel is architecture-independent and runs on riscv64 by construction. Upstream publishes directly to PyPI, satisfying the `release_provider: upstream` prerequisite for green.

Protobuf - yellow (optional) Release: Debian Gap: No upstream CI for riscv64 exists in any of the 26 workflow files (verified live: no "riscv" string in test_cpp.yml, test_python.yml, test_runner.yml, test_java.yml, or test_rust.yml). Debian sid ships protobuf 3.21.12-16 as "Installed" on riscv64 (built on rv-manda-03, verified live against [Debian buildd](https://buildd.debian.org/status/package.php?p=protobuf&suite=unstable)); the 3.21.12-16 patch set (verified live via Debian sources API) contains architecture-specific patches only for s390x, x32, hppa, loongarch64, and 32-bit platforms -- no riscv64-specific patch exists, qualifying for the clean-distro-build yellow floor. The optimization modifier does not apply: protobuf is a serialization framework whose correctness value is independent of SIMD acceleration.

FlatBuffers - yellow (optional) Release: Debian Gap: No upstream riscv64 CI exists in any of the six [.github/workflows files](https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/tree/master/.github/workflows) -- confirmed live by reading the full 644-line build.yml, which contains zero references to riscv64, qemu, or cross-compilation. Debian sid builds `libflatbuffers-dev 23.5.26+dfsg-4+b2` for riscv64 on `rv-osuosl-02` (status: Installed, verified 2026-08-28); the three Debian patches (setup-py.patch, s390x.patch, 8201.patch) are not riscv64-specific, confirming the build uses unmodified upstream source and qualifies for the yellow clean-distro-build floor. The library is uniformly scalar with no SIMD for any architecture, so the optimization-purpose modifier does not apply.

gRPC - orange (optional) Release: Arch Linux Gap: No riscv64 CI exists in any of the six GitHub Actions workflow files or the Bazel CI config (confirmed live). Distro packages are available (Arch Linux RISC-V at 1.81.0-1, Debian sid at 1.51.1-9+b1) but all require riscv64-specific env var overrides (GRPC_BUILD_WITH_BORING_SSL_ASM=0, GRPC_PYTHON_BUILD_SYSTEM_OPENSSL=1, -latomic workaround), keeping this at downstream-only orange rather than the cleaner yellow floor. Notably, issue [#41591](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/41591) requesting official riscv64 wheels was closed 2026-07-15 by maintainer sergiitk citing Google's OSS Support Policy which explicitly does not cover riscv64, indicating upstream has affirmatively declined formal riscv64 support rather than simply not having gotten around to it.

CPython - blue (critical) Release: RISE Gap: Live check of the CPython buildbot API confirms build #34 (2026-06-30) on builder 1377 ("riscv64 Ubuntu23 PR", tagged "unstable") ran a "test" step that completed with results=0 (success) on native riscv64 hardware (worker "onder-riscv64"), after build #33 (2026-06-29) failed the test step -- confirming the test suite executes but is not consistently passing. No riscv64 jobs exist in any of the 24 GitHub Actions workflow files (.github/workflows/). Upstream (python.org) publishes no riscv64 binaries; prebuilt riscv64 CPython binaries are provided by RISE via [riseproject-dev/python-versions](https://github.com/riseproject-dev/python-versions), placing this at blue (tests passed upstream on at least one run, but release is third-party). No builds have run in the ~59 days since #34, and the buildbot fires only on-demand per PR, not continuously.

glibc - yellow (critical) Release: Ubuntu Gap: The in-tree `scripts/build-many-glibcs.py` has three riscv64 cross-compile configurations with no `test_wrapper` and no QEMU invocation, confirmed by direct inspection. The Sourceware Buildbot riscv64 builders (IDs 293 and 336) do attempt test execution but every observable run returns `result=2` ("failed test (failure)"), and both builders are currently offline with empty masterids, as confirmed by [direct API query](https://builder.sourceware.org/buildbot/api/v2/builders/293) and [builder 336](https://builder.sourceware.org/buildbot/api/v2/builders/336). Ubuntu Noble 24.04 ships glibc 2.39, which predates the __SYSCALL_CLOBBERS vector-clobber fix (Sep 2025) and BZ#32932 (hwprobe prototype, glibc 2.42), creating real deployment risk on that LTS platform.

OpenSSL - blue (critical) Release: debian Gap: The [cross-compiles.yml](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/.github/workflows/cross-compiles.yml) workflow's riscv64 matrix entry carries no `tests: none` flag, so the "make all tests" step (excluding test_afalg) runs under QEMU on every push and EVP tests run on every PR -- confirmed by reading the actual workflow file today. Upstream publishes source-only tarballs for all architectures; Debian sid, Ubuntu 24.04, and Arch Linux RISC-V all carry current riscv64 packages. AES T-table constant-time fix PRs [#31080](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/31080) and [#31082](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/31082) remain open (state: open, merged_at: null as of 2026-08-28), but this is a security gap that does not affect the CI tier -- tests pass and blue is confirmed.

jemalloc - orange (critical) Release: Debian Gap: Live check of [linux-ci.yml](https://github.com/jemalloc/jemalloc/blob/dev/.github/workflows/linux-ci.yml) confirms zero riscv64 jobs across all 6 workflow files (only ubuntu-24.04 x86_64 and ubuntu-24.04-arm jobs). Debian sid ships libjemalloc2 5.3.1-2 for riscv64 with a single architecture-independent patch (dont-call-libstdcxx-internals.patch), qualifying for the clean-distro-build floor (yellow). However, jemalloc is explicitly an optimization-purpose allocator, and its RISC-V optimization level is absent -- no Zihintpause spinwait, no RVV, no RISC-V assembly, only a generic scalar fallback -- which caps the grade at orange (optimization-absent) per the color model.

tcmalloc - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: tcmalloc is an optimization-purpose allocator whose entire value proposition -- the lock-free per-CPU RSEQ slab -- is unavailable on riscv64: [`percpu.h`](https://github.com/google/tcmalloc/blob/master/tcmalloc/internal/percpu.h) guards `TCMALLOC_PERCPU_RSEQ_SUPPORTED_PLATFORM` to x86_64 and aarch64 only (confirmed live 2026-08-28), so riscv64 falls back to the slower per-thread path with no RISC-V-specific code anywhere in the project. There is also no riscv64 CI runner (no `LINUX_RISCV*` container in `ci/linux_docker_containers.sh`), and the project ships zero release artifacts of any kind; Debian/Ubuntu packages named `libtcmalloc-*` ship the unrelated `gperftools` codebase, not `google/tcmalloc`.

LZ4 - yellow (critical) Release: Debian Gap: The CI workflow at `.github/workflows/cross-platform.yml` runs `make platformTest` for riscv64 under QEMU, which executes the full correctness test suite (not build-only) -- establishing a blue primary grade. LZ4 is optimization-purpose (compression speed is its value proposition) and the primary hot paths `LZ4_FAST_DEC_LOOP` and `wildCopy64` remain disabled for riscv64 while enabled on x86 and arm64; the only merged RISC-V-specific code is the [Zicclsm unaligned-access fix (PR #1648)](https://github.com/lz4/lz4/pull/1648), a scalar portability optimization that does not cover the decompression fast path. Three independent PRs ([#1678](https://github.com/lz4/lz4/pull/1678), [#1686](https://github.com/lz4/lz4/pull/1686), [#1739](https://github.com/lz4/lz4/pull/1739)) and a new consolidated PR ([#1778](https://github.com/lz4/lz4/pull/1778)) to enable `LZ4_FAST_DEC_LOOP` and RVV acceleration remain open and unmerged as of 2026-08-28, capping the color at yellow (minimal optimization level -- Zicclsm scalar fix merged but primary hot paths absent).

zstd - yellow (critical) Release: debian Gap: The `qemu-consistency` job in [dev-short-tests.yml](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/blob/dev/.github/workflows/dev-short-tests.yml) runs `make clean check` on riscv64 via QEMU (baseline + RVV vlen=128/256/512), confirming full test execution and a blue primary CI grade. However, zstd is optimization-purpose: the Huffman 4-way decode loop remains gated to `__aarch64__` only (PR [#4622](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4622) still open), the sequence decode fast path is absent for riscv64 (PR [#4557](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4557) still open), and unaligned-access optimization for Zicclsm hardware is unmerged (PR [#4596](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4596) still open) -- all confirmed open as of 2026-08-28. Merged RVV code covers row-hash matching, ZSTD_copy16, and sequence conversion, but the dominant decompression hot paths remain scalar, placing optimization level at minimal and capping the grade to yellow.

snappy - yellow (optional) Release: debian Gap: The CI workflow [riscv64-qemu-test.yaml](https://github.com/google/snappy/blob/main/.github/workflows/riscv64-qemu-test.yaml) confirmed live: it builds and runs `make test` under QEMU on every push/PR, so the primary grade is **blue** (not build-only). However snappy is an optimization-purpose library (primary value = throughput) and the two most critical hot paths remain absent on riscv64: hardware CRC32 hash (SSE4.2/ARMv8 CRC on x86/arm64, scalar multiplicative fallback on riscv64) and V128 byte shuffle in the decompressor (SSSE3/NEON on x86/arm64, no vrgather RVV path on riscv64). Secondary paths do have RISC-V-specific code (Zicond branchless AdvanceToNextTag, 64-bit FindMatchLength, Zbb ctzll, partial RVV MemCopy64), but the primary differentiating operations are uncovered, so the optimization level is minimal and the cap reduces the final color from blue to yellow.
